investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never reached a schedulable state, causing the eval to time out and return an empty evidence object.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 137–144 seconds before the probe timed out, and no VM was ever assigned, so the expected-output contract fields vmIdPresent and remoteState were never populated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both nodes that match the pod's affinity, and preemption found no victims, indicating all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules. If the affinity was recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk, making exhaustion of the remaining 2 nodes more likely.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agents workload class: the cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If demand increased (e.g., concurrent eval runs or user workloads), those 2 nodes could be saturated simultaneously.

Lower probability — eval runner submitting duplicate or leaked pods from prior runs: if withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) failed to release VM slots from a previous run, those slots would still be consumed, contributing to exhaustion. No cleanup failure evidence is present in this packet.

Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never reached a schedulable state, causing the eval to time out and return an empty evidence object.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 137–144 seconds before the probe timed out, and no VM was ever assigned, so the expected-output contract fields vmIdPresent and remoteState were never populated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, confirming the agent VM was never created.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both nodes that match the pod's affinity, and preemption found no victims, indicating all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules. If the affinity was recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk, making exhaustion of the remaining 2 nodes more likely.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agents workload class: the cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If demand increased (e.g., concurrent eval runs or user workloads), those 2 nodes could be saturated simultaneously.

Lower probability — eval runner submitting duplicate or leaked pods from prior runs: if withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) failed to release VM slots from a previous run, those slots would still be consumed, contributing to exhaustion. No cleanup failure evidence is present in this packet.
